note: What the Fedora desktop payload must not contain. This file states the RULES only. It is never evidence: ops/inspect_payload.py answers every rule by looking at the artifact — listing the packaged tree, parsing the packaged distribution metadata and entry points, and running the packaged interpreter — and the answer is whatever it finds. A rule that finds nothing is a checked absence; a rule that finds something fails the build. Nothing here can make an exclusion succeed.

distributions.name: anthropic
distributions.why: Network client for a third-party model API. The desktop product must have no code path to a model somebody else runs, so neither the package nor its .dist-info may be in the payload.

distributions.name: hf_xet
distributions.why: Hugging Face Xet transfer backend. It exists only to download model data at runtime; a packaged, offline application ships its weights and must never fetch any.

distributions.name: pip
distributions.why: Installs more software at runtime into a tree that is read-only on the target.

distributions.name: setuptools
distributions.why: Build-time machinery; nothing in the packaged application builds anything.

modules.name: anthropic
modules.why: The hosted Anthropic SDK. Must not be importable from the packaged interpreter.

modules.name: hf_xet
modules.why: Runtime download backend; not required by the approved self-hosted runtime (model2vec loads the bundled weights from disk).

modules.name: huggingface_hub.inference
modules.why: InferenceClient/AsyncInferenceClient and the whole hosted inference surface, including huggingface_hub.inference._providers — a registry of ~20 third-party inference-provider adapters (together, replicate, fal_ai, openai, cohere, groq, ...). Every one of them is a hosted generation path.

modules.name: huggingface_hub.inference._providers
modules.why: The hosted inference-provider registry itself, named separately so its absence is asserted in its own right and not only as a consequence of its parent package.

modules.name: app.llm_hosted
modules.why: The repository's hosted-generation plug-in (Anthropic SDK provider and Claude CLI provider). Present for the web product, deliberately not copied into the desktop payload; app.llm discovers it at selection time, so its absence removes the implementations, the registration and the selection keys together.

attributes.why: huggingface_hub exposes its hosted client through a lazy module __getattr__, so file absence alone does not prove the attribute cannot be reached. Access must raise.

pathPatterns.why: Adapter sources and bytecode for the hosted inference providers.
Legacy hosted inference client module and its bytecode.
The hosted plug-in module and its bytecode.

entryPointPatterns.why: An entry point is a registration: it names an implementation a plug-in host can load without the application ever importing it explicitly. None may point at a hosted provider, at a hosted inference CLI, or at the removed inference tree.

providerIdentifiers.why: The provider name the Anthropic implementation reports. It must not be selectable, and no packaged module may name it.
The provider name the Claude CLI implementation reports. Same rule.

selectionKeys.why: BRF_LLM=api selected the Anthropic provider. In the packaged payload it must fall through to `none`.
BRF_LLM=cli selected the Claude CLI provider. Same rule.

selectionEnvironments.label: auto with a hosted API key exported
selectionEnvironments.why: The historical auto-detection trigger. Must yield `none`, not a hosted provider.

selectionEnvironments.label: auto with a `claude` executable on PATH
selectionEnvironments.why: The other historical auto-detection trigger: a logged-in CLI on the machine. Must yield `none`.

selectionEnvironments.label: forced hosted API key
selectionEnvironments.why: An explicit attempt to force the hosted provider must not find one.

selectionEnvironments.label: forced hosted CLI
selectionEnvironments.why: An explicit attempt to force the CLI provider must not find one.

filenameScan.why: Every path in the whole payload — package directories, modules, bytecode, metadata directories, data files — swept for a forbidden name. Cheap, exhaustive, and it cannot be satisfied by anything except the files actually being gone. Scoped to huggingface_hub's inference tree rather than any directory called `inference`, because model2vec ships a local `model2vec/inference` head-pipeline that runs entirely on this machine and is not a hosted path.

textScan.why: A strict content sweep over the parts of the payload this project authors and can therefore hold to a no-forbidden-names standard: the packaged product code and the built desktop UI. Every match must be an explicitly declared reference (see declaredReferences) or the inspection fails.

scan.why: The built desktop UI. A shipped provider label would be an exposed hosted identifier even though it is not an implementation.

notScanned.why: Third-party sources are held to the structural rules above (distributions, modules, attributes, pathPatterns, entryPointPatterns, filenameScan, import probes) rather than to a content sweep. huggingface_hub legitimately keeps guarded optional imports of hf_xet and dangling lazy-attribute entries for the removed inference tree; editing vendored sources to erase those names would risk the approved embedder for no gain, and the probes below prove that none of them can resolve. See guardedOptionalImports.
A compiled binary is not a content surface a text sweep can reason about; its one forbidden literal is declared, counted and asserted in declaredReferences instead.

guardedOptionalImports.why: huggingface_hub imports hf_xet lazily behind an availability check, so its sources still name it. With the distribution absent the check is False and the import is unreachable; this probe proves that rather than asserting it.

declaredReferences.classification: environment-scrub argument in the compiled shell
declaredReferences.why: src-tauri/src/main.rs removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the backend child process's environment. The literal is therefore present in the compiled binary as the name of a variable being DELETED, not as an implementation, an import, a registration or a selectable identifier. It is declared here so the inspection reports it explicitly instead of quietly not looking; the count is asserted, so a second, undeclared occurrence still fails.
declaredReferences.retainedBecause: Defence in depth costs nothing and removing a security scrub to make a string search pass would weaken the product to flatter the evidence.

declaredReferences.classification: default value of the per-tenant `aiModel` setting
declaredReferences.why: Settings.aiModel is a tenant preference, not a provider: it names no implementation, registers nothing, and selects no provider. The desktop never uses it for generation — app.desktop.apply_model_runtime always exports the configured ModelRuntimeConfig.model (default gemma4:e12b) and app.answer prefers the provider's own model over the setting — and the desktop UI has no control that displays it. The selection probes below assert the reported generation model, so the claim is checked rather than argued.
declaredReferences.retainedBecause: Changing a persisted per-tenant default is a persistence change with no packaging necessity, and it would break the repository's hosted dev/eval default, which this repair must preserve. Recorded as a known residual instead of quietly rewritten.

requiredPresent.why: The approved self-hosted embedder. The exclusions must not have damaged it.
model2vec imports it (model cards, persistence). Pruning the hosted inference surface must leave the package itself working.
Reached transitively by model2vec's persistence path. It imports huggingface_hub._inference_endpoints at module scope, which is why that one module is retained — see retainedModules.

retainedModules.why: A management dataclass for HF Inference Endpoints, not an inference-provider adapter. huggingface_hub.hf_api imports it at module scope, and model2vec reaches hf_api through its model-card path, so removing it breaks the approved embedder outright (verified: ModuleNotFoundError from model2vec.persistence).
retainedModules.provenInert: Its only route to a hosted client is InferenceEndpoint.client / .async_client, which import huggingface_hub.inference._client — removed. The inspection constructs the class and asserts that both properties raise instead of returning a client.
